name: pymodelica-scope
description: Simulate the Modelica .mo file you are editing and see its trajectory, in an interactive chart inside VS Code.

pymodelica.runtime.description: Which runtime simulates the model. 'auto' picks the fastest available (Python today; a Rust/C interpreter later).

pymodelica.python.description: Command that runs a Python with `modelica` importable. The simulator script and arguments are appended.

pymodelica.stop.description: Stop time for the simulation. 0 means use the model's own (its sibling .toml's [simulate].stop, else 10). You can also change it live in the panel.

pymodelica.autoStopMax.description: How far the automatic stops ('→ event', '⇥ settle') may probe past the current stop before giving up. 0 means ten times the current stop. A cap, so a model that never settles comes back in seconds.

pymodelica.library.description: Extra .mo files or folders to load for dependencies (a sibling 'library/' folder is loaded automatically). E.g. 'examples/library' for the corpus models.

pymodelica.cwd.description: Working directory to run the simulator in. Empty means the workspace folder of the .mo file.

pymodelica.simulateOnSave.description: Re-simulate the model when you save a .mo file (only while the Scope panel is open).

pymodelica.standardLibrary.description: Load the bundled slice of the Modelica Standard Library, so a model that references the real Modelica.* names (Electrical.Analog, Blocks, Mechanics, Thermal) resolves without configuration. A curated subset, not the whole MSL.
